nodes.name: Gulab Chand Tejwani
nodes.summary: Power BI practitioner and author of an empirical DAX performance study analyzing 5,247 DAX measures across 89 production reports, identifying 5 performance-killing patterns.

nodes.name: Md Mizanur Rahman Nayan
nodes.summary: PL-300 certified Power BI practitioner specializing in streak detection, gaps-and-islands problems, and practical DAX tutorials with real-world datasets.

nodes.name: Marco Russo and Alberto Ferrari
nodes.summary: SQLBI co-founders and primary authors of DAX reference documentation covering calculation groups, performance optimization, and advanced patterns.

nodes.name: SELECTEDMEASURE
nodes.summary: DAX function used inside calculation items that references whichever measure is currently being evaluated by the visual.

nodes.name: ALL Function
nodes.summary: DAX function that removes all filters on a table or column, ignoring slicers and report filters entirely.

nodes.name: ALLSELECTED Function
nodes.summary: DAX function that removes filters only at the visual level while respecting user slicer selections that are currently active.

nodes.name: CALCULATE Function
nodes.summary: Core DAX context-modifier that evaluates an expression in a modified filter context.

nodes.name: Calculation Group
nodes.summary: Power BI feature that allows a single column to apply multiple calculation variants (e.g., MTD, QTD, YTD) to any measure without duplicating measure definitions.

nodes.name: Calculation Item
nodes.summary: Individual named expression within a calculation group that wraps a measure using SELECTEDMEASURE, applying a specific calculation variant.

nodes.name: Tabular Editor
nodes.summary: Free external tool for creating and managing calculation groups in Power BI, connecting directly to the in-memory model.

nodes.name: DAX Studio
nodes.summary: Free external tool for querying, analyzing, and debugging DAX expressions, useful for testing calculation item expressions before deployment.

nodes.name: ALM Toolkit
nodes.summary: Free external tool for comparing and deploying tabular models between environments, useful for promoting calculation groups across dev/staging/prod.

nodes.name: ISINSCOPE
nodes.summary: DAX function that returns true when the specified column is in the current filter context as a grouping column, used for per-level conditional formatting in measures.

nodes.name: ISATLEVEL
nodes.summary: DAX function used in visual calculations to detect if the current row is at a specific hierarchy level, operating on the visual rowset rather than the full model.

nodes.name: COLLAPSE and COLLAPSEALL
nodes.summary: Visual calculation functions for navigating up a hierarchy: COLLAPSE moves one level up, COLLAPSEALL collapses to grand total.

nodes.name: Dynamic Format String
nodes.summary: Calculation group feature that overrides the format of the underlying measure using a format string expression, enabling conditional percentage, currency, or custom formatting.

nodes.name: Unnecessary Iterators Pattern
nodes.summary: Using SUMX/SUM(A[Col]) instead of SUM(A[Col]) is the most common DAX performance killer, affecting 364 measures (41%) with an average 19.5x speedup when fixed.

nodes.name: Calculated Columns for Aggregation
nodes.summary: Using calculated columns for aggregation instead of measures consumes 890 MB of memory and adds 22 minutes of refresh time, with 67% memory reduction possible after fixing.

nodes.name: RELATED in Iterators Performance Impact
nodes.summary: Using RELATED() inside iterators causes 14.2s to 0.9s execution times, an average 14.9x speedup when refactored to avoid row-by-row lookups.

nodes.name: Nested CALCULATE plus FILTER(ALL())
nodes.summary: Nested CALCULATE with FILTER(ALL()) patterns show 15.7s to 1.3s execution, averaging 12.1x speedup when simplified.

nodes.name: ALL vs REMOVEFILTERS When REMOVEFILTERS Works
nodes.summary: Using ALL() when REMOVEFILTERS() would suffice causes 12.8s to 1.1s execution, averaging 11.6x speedup when corrected.

nodes.name: Calculation Items Require Direct Measure Reference
nodes.summary: A calculation item only activates when the expression contains a direct measure reference; if there is no measure to target, the calculation item is silently skipped.

nodes.name: ALL Ignores All Filters; ALLSELECTED Respects Slicer Context
nodes.summary: ALL ignores all filters including slicers and report filters, while ALLSELECTED respects the current user slicer context. Using the wrong one returns either the grand total or an incorrect filtered value.

nodes.name: noSelectionExpression Fires When CG Column Has Zero Filters
nodes.summary: The noSelectionExpression property fires only when the calculation group column has no filters at all, including indirect cross-filters, distinct from empty selection which produces zero rows from an active filter.

nodes.name: multipleOrEmptySelectionExpression Handles Both Zero and Multiple Items
nodes.summary: The multipleOrEmptySelectionExpression property intercepts both zero visible items and two or more visible items in a single event, providing a unified hook for both conditions.

nodes.name: ISINSCOPE and ISATLEVEL Serve Different Architectural Locations
nodes.summary: ISINSCOPE operates in semantic model measures and requires ownership of the model; ISATLEVEL operates in visual calculations and is required when working with shared datasets or when logic needs data outside the visual.

nodes.name: Conditional Variance Returns BLANK for -100% Variance
nodes.summary: A naive Actual/Budget - 1 variance formula returns -100% when no budget is assigned, misleading users. The fix returns BLANK() when variance is -100% or worse or when budget is blank.

nodes.name: Gaps and Islands Pattern Enables Streak Detection
nodes.summary: The gaps and islands pattern detects consecutive active periods (streaks) in DAX using a rank subtraction trick, enabling detection of consecutive active days, customer streaks, and similar sequences.

nodes.name: Tabular Editor Is the Required Tool for Creating Calculation Groups
nodes.summary: Tabular Editor is the only tool required to create calculation groups; DAX Studio and ALM Toolkit are recommended but optional additions.

nodes.name: Calculation Groups Make All Measures Variant Data Type
nodes.summary: When a calculation group is added to a model, all measures become variant data type, which can break dynamic format string reuse patterns where one measure's format string references another measure.

nodes.name: CG Selection Properties Require Compatibility Level 1605
nodes.summary: The noSelectionExpression and multipleOrEmptySelectionExpression properties require compatibility level 1605 minimum; Tabular Editor hides these properties if CL is below 1605.

edges.description: Unnecessary iterators pattern was identified through Tejwani's study of 5,247 DAX measures across 89 production reports.
Calculated column aggregation pattern was identified in Tejwani's empirical performance study.
RELATED() in iterators performance impact was measured in Tejwani's study with 14.9x average speedup.
Nested CALCULATE + FILTER(ALL()) pattern was documented in Tejwani's 5-pattern performance analysis.
ALL when REMOVEFILTERS works pattern was identified as one of the five performance-killing patterns in Tejwani's study.
Gaps and islands streak detection technique was documented by Nayan using a 6-step algorithm with rank subtraction trick.
The requirement for a direct measure reference exemplifies the behavior of SELECTEDMEASURE() which cannot resolve without an active measure.
The silent-skip behavior is a property of calculation items, which only apply when SELECTEDMEASURE() can resolve.
The measure reference requirement is a foundational constraint of the calculation group feature.
ALL's behavior of ignoring all filters exemplifies the scope difference between ALL and ALLSELECTED.
ALLSELECTED's behavior of respecting user slicer context exemplifies the scope difference from ALL.
ALL and ALLSELECTED are used inside CALCULATE to modify the filter context, making CALCULATE the context for understanding scope differences.
The noSelectionExpression property exemplifies the selection-context handling capability of calculation groups.
The multipleOrEmptySelectionExpression property exemplifies a gap-closing feature in calculation group selection handling.
MultipleOrEmptySelectionExpression extends the same selection-context interception concept as noSelectionExpression.
The architectural decision table exemplifies when ISINSCOPE in a measure is the correct choice versus ISATLEVEL.
The decision workflow exemplifies ISATLEVEL's preferred use cases for shared datasets and visual-only logic.
The conditional variance pattern uses CALCULATE and DIVIDE to implement the blank-on-minus-100 behavior.
Tabular Editor being the required tool exemplifies its central role in the calculation group creation workflow.
Tabular Editor is required for creation while DAX Studio supports validation, showing complementary roles.
Tabular Editor is required for creation while ALM Toolkit supports deployment across environments.
Dynamic format string is a property of calculation items within calculation groups.
The variant data type side effect exemplifies a gotcha that emerges when a calculation group is added to the model.
The variant data type side effect can break dynamic format string reuse patterns, contradicting assumptions about format string independence.
Compatibility level 1605 requirement exemplifies a version gate on advanced calculation group features.
COLLAPSE/COLLAPSEALL provide a report-layer equivalent to CALCULATE + REMOVEFILTERS that complements calculation group time intelligence.
